plan_a_advantages: Consistent easy running volume could be beneficial for maintaining a base level of fitness.
The high number of rest days might be suitable for an athlete recovering from injury or needing significant recovery.
plan_b_advantages: Includes a dedicated long run, simulating trail race distances and building endurance.
Incorporates cross-training, providing a low-impact alternative for maintaining fitness and preventing overuse injuries.
More varied workout types (long run, cross-training) offer a broader stimulus for adaptation.
reasoning: Plan B is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. While Plan A focuses heavily on very short, consistent easy runs, it lacks a dedicated long run or any structured interval or hill work – crucial elements for improving trail running speed. Plan B incorporates a longer run to build endurance and simulates trail conditions, alongside a cross-training session to maintain fitness without excessive impact. The inclusion of a 60-minute long run is significantly more beneficial for developing the sustained effort required in trail races than the consistent, but ultimately limited, easy runs in Plan A. Furthermore, the cross-training session in Plan B addresses the need for varied training stimulus.
